summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results comparing Redwood to their current baseline provider. Discussion focused on latency p50/p95, throughput at various batch sizes and context lengths, variability causes, and next steps to run 8k-context tests and plan a canary Dedicated run. Security intake and scheduling were reconfirmed.
topics: Next steps: additional tests, spreadsheet share, canary scheduling
transcript: [00:00] Marcus Lee: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Marcus from Redwood here. Today is the weekly POC sync - we'll go through the benchmark sheet, call out any anomalies, and align on next steps.
[00:10] Sara Kim: Hi everyone, Sara here. We got Daniel and Alex on my side. We ran your test deck overnight, so curious to see the comparison to BaselineCloudAI.
[00:18] Daniel Ortiz: Morning. The baseline runs are the ones we use in prod, so we're mainly looking at p95 tail latency and sustained throughput.
[00:27] Priya Raman: Great, I pulled the latest runs into benchmark_v3.xlsx, link in the invite notes. Quick note: the runs were on 4k context unless noted otherwise.
[00:40] Alex Chen: We also care about variance during bursts; our traffic is spiky. p95s are more important than p50s for us.

[00:51] Marcus Lee: Totally. Ok jumping into slide 1 of the sheet Redwood vs BaselineCloudAI, 4k context, batch sizes of 1,4,8. p50 for Redwood is about 120ms, p95 around 420ms on hosted, while Baseline is p50 150ms, p95 680ms.
[01:10] Sara Kim: Wait p95 680? That's pretty high. Is that with caching enabled on their side?

[01:16] Priya Raman: We matched as much config as possible but there are infra differences. One place to call out: Baseline was running with their standard autoscale policy which caused cold starts in some runs.
[01:26] Daniel Ortiz: Are these warm-cache numbers? We want steady-state mostly.
[01:31] Priya Raman: The sheet includes both cold and warm segments; the 'steady_state' tab shows warm runs only. In steady_state Redwood p95 drops to ~320ms.
[01:42] Alex Chen: That's promising. How about throughput at batch size 8?
[01:46] Marcus Lee: At batch 8, tokens/sec for Redwood is about 2100 on the test workload, Baseline was ~1600. Note these are synthetic prompts approximating your average user flows.
[01:58] Sara Kim: Do you account for KV cache / prefix cache? We have a lot of repeated prefixes in our use case.

[02:04] Priya Raman: Yes, we enabled prefix caching in the Redwood runtime for these runs. Small note ������ sometimes the transcription engine shows K-V cash in the logs, but that's just a naming glitch, it's K/V cache functionality.
[02:18] Daniel Ortiz: Cool. We saw occasional outlier runs around 1.2s p95 in your logs �� what's the cause?
[02:24] Priya Raman: Those correspond to a particular node that had a kernel swap during a GPU driver update; we flagged them. We re-ran the subset without that node and the outliers disappeared.
[02:36] Marcus Lee: Also worth noting, our kernel selector adapts for sequence length distribution. When we forced long sequences we see different kernel paths and the p95 jumps, which is expected.
[02:47] Alex Chen: That brings me to context length �� you tested 1k, 4k, and you mentioned 8k is pending. How much does Redwood degrade at 8k?

[02:54] Priya Raman: Preliminary internal runs show about 30-40% latency increase at 8k on hosted config, but throughput per-GPU can be better once you tune batch windows. We need to run customer-specific workload to be sure.
[03:08] Sara Kim: Ok we definitely need the 8k numbers � many of our edge cases have long context. Can you run those against Baseline as well?
[03:14] Marcus Lee: Yes, we'll queue that. Priya will run 8k-context benchmark parity tests and share raw logs.
[03:21] Daniel Ortiz: On Dedicated vs Hosted, what were you using for these runs? Dedicated pool or Redwood hosted shared?
[03:26] Priya Raman: These runs were on our hosted tier with pinned model versions. We can replicate on Dedicated; in fact a canary on a small Dedicated pool is our next step.
[03:36] Marcus Lee: Quick tradeoff: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor variance, gives more consistent p95 but costs more. We can propose a small Dedicated canary to validate at scale.
[03:46] Alex Chen: Cost is a concern, but reliability is higher priority. If Dedicated flattens the tail we'll consider it.
[03:53] Sara Kim: Security check � we started the SOC2 intake, there are questions about KMS and audit logs. Do you have an intake doc?
[03:59] Marcus Lee: Yes, shared security-deck.pdf in the folder. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and detailed audit logs; Priya can follow up with the SOC2 contact.
[04:10] Priya Raman: I'll be the primary for technical security questions. I'll also attach the sample audit log format. Note: our private deployment supports customer-managed HSM too.
[04:20] Daniel Ortiz: Good. Also ask about data residency � some of our prod traffic must stay within EU-West; can Redwood route?
[04:26] Marcus Lee: Yes, region routing is supported. We can pin requests to region and fall back policies are configurable. We'll document the routing policy options in the runbook.
[04:36] Sara Kim: Back to benchmarks � were you testing with function calling and streaming enabled? That changes the tokenization/latency profile a bit.
[04:43] Priya Raman: For parity we disabled extras like function calling; we did one streaming-enabled run (sheet tab streaming) � results were similar but more variability at the application layer.

[04:55] Marcus Lee: A couple of notes in the sheet: 1) Baseline had higher cold-starts due to their container spin-up, 2) Redwood's batching heuristics reduced p95 when enabled, 3) quantization profile used was int8 for both where supported.
[05:10] Alex Chen: Can you send exact command lines and environment? We want to reproduce internally.
[05:14] Priya Raman: Yes I'll share the runbook with the docker/runner commands and the perf logs link. It's in the invite as runbook.md but I'll attach a detailed version.
[05:24] Sara Kim: Regarding the 1.2s outliers, can you correlate with autoscale events? We saw spikes when requests hit a new node.

[05:30] Marcus Lee: We did correlate � those outliers aligned with autoscale cold starts on the Baseline runs; Redwood's tested runs used a warmed pool to show steady-state. We'll add an explicit cold-start section to the sheet.
[05:41] Daniel Ortiz: One nit: the prompt shapes in the synthetic workload don't capture some of our multi-turn flows. Could we run a small replay of real traces?
[05:48] Priya Raman: Absolutely. If you can share sanitized traces we'll run them and include results under 'customer_replay' tab.
[05:55] Sara Kim: We'll prepare that � need to strip PII first. Might take a couple days.
[06:00] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. For immediate next steps: I'll share benchmark_v3 and runbook, Priya will run 8k tests and replay traces when provided, and we'll propose canary slots for mid-May.
[06:10] Alex Chen: Quick question on metrics: do you provide per-route token-level cost breakdown? We want to estimate unit economics.
[06:16] Marcus Lee: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route cost and latency breakdowns; we'll share a demo link and a sample CSV export.
[06:24] Daniel Ortiz: Competitor checks � BaselineCloudAI said they'd lower price if we commit longer term. We want to see if Redwood's latency/throughput delta is worth switching.
[06:33] Priya Raman: Understood. We'll try to provide the 8k numbers and a cost/run comparison so you can model switching cost vs performance benefit.
[06:41] Sara Kim: Anything on model accuracy/regression? We care about output quality when switching quantization profiles.
[06:47] Marcus Lee: Good point � we ran basic evals using your eval set; accuracy delta was within tolerance for int8 quantization. We'll attach the eval summaries to the sheet.
[06:58] Alex Chen: For the canary, we want a rollback plan. How does Redwood handle A/B and automatic fallback?
[07:05] Priya Raman: We support canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and region failover. We'll include the rollback steps in the canary plan.

[07:14] Marcus Lee: Ok wrapping up � recapping next steps and owners verbally: Marcus share sheet/runbook, Priya run 8k and replay tests, Sara provide traces and SOC2 contact, Alex give infra diagram. Any other asks?
[07:28] Sara Kim: That's it from our side. Thanks for the thorough review.
[07:32] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the 8k numbers.
[07:35] Marcus Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links and a proposed canary schedule. End call.
